title: Proud Tek Certifications — ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001, OEKO-TEX, RoHS, REACH and CE test reports
summary: Shenzhen Proud Tek Co., Ltd holds three audited management-system certifications — ISO 9001:2015 (quality), ISO 14001:2015 (environment) and ISO 45001:2018 (occupational health & safety) — issued by Anhui Certification and Inspection Co., Ltd and valid to 09 June 2029, plus an OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 certificate (Hohenstein, product class II) for our UHF laundry tag and sample-based RoHS, REACH SVHC and CE (EN 62311) test reports. Every certificate number, issuer, scope and validity is published below so your supplier-qualification team can verify them without contacting us first. Read the scope line before relying on any of them: the ISO certificates cover our sales and supplier-management operation — production runs on contracted partner lines — and the RoHS, REACH and CE documents are sample-based lab reports on the specific articles they name. The page then sets out the air-interface standards every SKU is built to and how radio approvals are handled per destination market.
heroPoints: Three audited ISO management systems, published with certificate numbers: ISO 9001:2015 (98026Q00274R000), ISO 14001:2015 (98026E00200R000) and ISO 45001:2018 (98026S00203R000), all valid to 09 June 2029.

Certified scope, stated plainly: the sales service of smart cards (PVC and wooden cards) and RFID tags, held by Shenzhen Proud Tek Co., Ltd; production runs on contracted partner lines, whose own certificates we supply on request.

Product-level proof: OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 certificate 23.HCN.97349 (Hohenstein, product class II) for our UHF laundry tag — checked valid in the OEKO-TEX Label Check on 2 September 2026 — plus sample-based RoHS, REACH SVHC and CE (EN 62311) test reports with their numbers below.

sections.title: Air-interface and protocol standards
sections.intro: Every Proud Tek SKU is built to a published air-interface standard — we do not ship 'compatible' inlays that read only on a specific reader brand. This is the basis for reader-fleet interoperability across deployment lifetimes.

features.title: HF — ISO/IEC 14443
features.text: 13.56 MHz proximity cards and tags. Type A (MIFARE Classic / Plus / DESFire / Ultralight / NTAG) and Type B (CIPURSE, ePassport) supported.

features.title: Vicinity — ISO/IEC 15693
features.text: 13.56 MHz longer-range cards and labels (ICODE SLIX, ICODE SLIX2, M24LR). Most library and asset-tracking deployments run on this.

features.title: UHF — ISO/IEC 18000-6C / EPC Gen2
features.text: 860-960 MHz EPC Gen2 / Gen2v2 inlays — UCODE 8/9, Monza 4/R6/M7xx, Higgs-3/4/9/EC, Quanray QY9300. RAIN RFID Alliance interoperable.

features.title: LF — ISO/IEC 11784/11785
features.text: 125 kHz / 134.2 kHz low-frequency tags. EM4200 / 4305, {chip:atmel-t5577:name}, HID Prox-compatible inlays for legacy access-control retrofits.

features.title: NFC Forum — Type 2, Type 4, Type 5
features.text: NTAG 213/215/216/424 DNA, MIFARE DESFire / Ultralight, ICODE SLIX — NDEF compliant, tested against NFC Forum reference devices.

features.title: Industry-specific encoding
features.text: GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard 2.3, ISO/IEC 15962 (RFID data protocol), AIM Global URI templates, Auburn ARC inlay performance specifications.

sections.title: Material and substance compliance
sections.intro: Material compliance is evidenced by sample-based laboratory reports on specific articles, published above with their numbers, rather than by a blanket catalogue claim. SVHC list updates from the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) trigger a review of the affected articles within 30 days of publication.
bullets: RoHS (Directive 2011/65/EU + 2015/863 amendment) — sample-based Certificate of Compliance XKS2025R01150076 on an RFID card; testing on your own specification can be commissioned for a project-critical file.
REACH SVHC — screening report XKS2025R10150032E (250 substances, RFID keyfob, all below the reporting limit); the ECHA Candidate List is reviewed at each update.
Conflict minerals — CMRT (Conflict Minerals Reporting Template) available for buyers under SEC Dodd-Frank Section 1502 compliance.
Halogen-free / PVC-free options — recycled-PVC and PVC-free substrate stocks available on request.
Battery Regulation 2023/1542 — supporting documentation for tags containing batteries (active RFID, BLE beacons).

sections.title: Radio approvals by destination market
sections.intro: Passive RFID inlays and cards are unpowered and generally do not require radio-type approval — it is RFID readers and active / battery devices that do. For those, radio approval is per-device-per-market. We process the approvals a program actually needs (FCC in the US, CE in the EU, MIC in Japan, CCC in China, ANATEL in Brazil and so on) rather than claiming blanket coverage; ask us which approvals apply to your specific SKUs.

comparePanel.afterHeading: How Proud Tek actually handles it
before: Inlays from China can ship into any market — no extra paperwork needed.
FCC and CE are equivalent and one covers the other.
Test reports are 'available somewhere' but not part of the shipment.
Radio approvals apply to the chip, not the finished product.
Approval cost is a per-shipment overhead the buyer absorbs.
after: Each destination market needs its own approval for powered devices — FCC (US), CE (EU), MIC (Japan), CCC (China), ANATEL (Brazil), etc.; passive tags and cards generally need none.
FCC Part 15 and CE EN 300 330 / EN 302 208 are independent regulatory regimes with different test methods.
For passive cards we publish the EN 62311 RF-exposure test report (BCTC2509165308-1E); CE marking remains a manufacturer declaration supported by reports like this one.
Approval is per finished device; antenna and substrate matter. Reader devices are approved per device per market, with the report supplied.
Baseline documentation ships with the order; specialty market approvals (e.g., ANATEL) are priced into the programme if applicable.

sections.title: Regional regulatory readiness
sections.intro: Two pieces of EU legislation that are reshaping the RFID supply chain are the EU Digital Product Passport (under Ecodesign Regulation 2024/1781, rolling out from 2026) and the Battery Regulation 2023/1542. We track both closely because our customer base is heavily weighted toward EU-bound programs.
bullets: EU DPP — NTAG 213/215/216/424 DNA NFC inlays and UCODE 8/9 UHF inlays meet the air-interface and memory requirements anticipated by ESPR delegated acts.
EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 — Technical files for RFID-tagged industrial and EV batteries supported; QR + NFC dual-encoding available.
GS1 Digital Link — URI-formatted EPC encoding for products that need to resolve to a brand-owner web endpoint.
Walmart RFID source-tagging mandate — Auburn ARC-graded UHF inlays for Walmart category programs.
USDA / FDA traceability — RFID solutions for food and pharmaceutical lot tracking compatible with FSMA 204 and DSCSA requirements.
FCC IDs and CE technical files — maintained per SKU and provided as part of the documentation pack.

sections.title: Third-party certified test reports
sections.intro: When a program requires third-party attestation beyond our internal QA, we route the test through one of the major laboratories. Lead time and cost vary by certification scope; we absorb baseline cost as part of annual-volume agreements when justified.
bullets: TÜV Rheinland — full-spectrum electrical, mechanical and material certification.
SGS — material composition (RoHS / REACH), radio compliance, factory audits (we do not currently hold an SGS factory audit).
Intertek — quality assurance, social compliance, Sedex SMETA audits.
Bureau Veritas — supply-chain audits, regulatory advisory, factory inspection.
Auburn University RFID Lab — independent UHF inlay performance grading (ARC).
Customer-named laboratory — testing routed through a buyer-specified lab when program requires it.

faq.question: Can we get a copy of your ISO 9001 certificate before placing an order?
faq.answer: You do not have to ask. The number is published on this page: ISO 9001:2015, certificate 98026Q00274R000, issued by Anhui Certification and Inspection Co., Ltd to Shenzhen Proud Tek Co., Ltd on 10 June 2026 and valid to 09 June 2029. Look it up on the CNCA national register at cnca.gov.cn. The certified scope is the sales service of smart cards (PVC and wooden cards) and RFID tags — production runs on contracted partner lines, so if you need a production-scope certificate naming a plant address, request the partner line's own documentation and we will supply it during quotation. A PDF of any of the certificates is available on request.

faq.question: Are your radio approvals 'self-declared' or are they third-party tested?
faq.answer: Passive RFID cards and tags are unpowered and generally need no radio-type approval; for them we publish a third-party EN 62311 RF-exposure test report (BCTC2509165308-1E, Shenzhen BCTC Testing Co., Ltd). CE marking is a manufacturer declaration supported by reports like that one — it is not a certification issued by a notified body. Reader devices and active tags are approved per device per market (FCC, CE, MIC, CCC, ANATEL), and the report for the specific device ships with the order.

faq.question: How does your REACH SVHC declaration stay current?
faq.answer: ECHA publishes SVHC list updates twice yearly. Our current report is a sample-based screening of 250 Candidate List substances on an RFID keyfob (XKS2025R10150032E, Oct 2025); when the list changes we review the affected articles within 30 days, and testing on your own specification can be commissioned for a project-critical file.

faq.question: Do you support Walmart RFID source-tagging compliance?
faq.answer: Yes. We manufacture Auburn ARC-graded UHF inlays for Walmart-mandate category programs. Buyers receive ARC grading documentation and SGTIN-96 encoding per GS1 EPC TDS 2.3 standard. Walmart Retail Link RFID Supplier Enablement Sandbox testing is supported as part of program ramp-up.

faq.question: Are your products RoHS and REACH compliant for the EU and US markets?
faq.answer: Our evidence is sample-based: a RoHS 2.0 Certificate of Compliance on an RFID card (XKS2025R01150076) and a REACH SVHC screening report on an RFID keyfob (XKS2025R10150032E), both published above. They evidence the tested articles, not every SKU, so for a project-critical compliance file we commission testing on your exact specification and ship the report with the order. California Prop 65 declarations are prepared per SKU on request for consumer-facing SKUs distributed into California; they are not published here.

faq.question: What if my buyer requires a certification you do not currently hold?
faq.answer: Mention it on the initial inquiry. What we hold is ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 — numbers and scope published above — plus OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 (23.HCN.97349) for our UHF laundry tag and sample-based RoHS, REACH SVHC and CE test reports, all with numbers above. Everything beyond that, including IATF 16949, ISO 13485, AS9100D, ISO 27001 and social-compliance frameworks such as Sedex SMETA, BSCI and RBA, is something we arrange through the relevant institute or auditor for a specific programme rather than something we already carry. Lead time and cost depend on the scope; for high-volume annual programs we typically absorb the baseline cost. If a certificate is a hard gate for your category, say so early — it changes the timeline.
